plainTranslation: Complementary emotional opposites. One needs space where the other needs closeness; one processes aloud where the other goes quiet. Failure mode: each reading the other's style as rejection. Name your needs explicitly - the contrast can balance you once you stop taking it personally.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.
note: Synced from authored synastry bundle synastry-authored__19_ (2).json.
summaryDeep: Your emotional needs and habits keep missing each other. What soothes one of you unsettles the other. Learn each other's actual comfort, not the one you'd assume.
tension: The real challenge is assuming that your way is the right way. When your emotional needs become the standard, the other person can start to feel unseen, even when your intentions are good. Over time, both people may end up feeling misunderstood by someone who genuinely cares.
advice: The opportunity here is learning to get curious instead of making assumptions. Ask what helps. Pay attention to what actually settles the other person rather than what would settle you. The more you learn each other's emotional language, the less time you spend missing each other and the more time you spend feeling truly understood.
summaryShort: Your emotional needs and habits keep missing each other.
